| ECS blue/green deployments through CodeDeploy                                                 | You can now use CloudFormation to perform ECS blue/green deployments through CodeDeploy.<br>Blue/green deployments are a safe deployment strategy provided by AWS CodeDeploy for<br>minimizing interruptions caused by changing application versions. For more<br>information, see [Performing ECS blue/green deployments through CodeDeploy using<br>CloudFormation](blue-green.md "blue-green.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | May 19, 2020      |
| CloudFormation StackSets Region availability                                                  | CloudFormation StackSets is now available in the AWS GovCloud (US-West)<br>Region.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | May 18, 2020      |
| AWS CloudFormation StackSets integrates with AWS Organizations                                | You can now use StackSets to centrally manage deployments to all the accounts in<br>your organization or specific organizational units (OUs) in AWS Organizations. You can enable<br>automatic deployments to any new accounts added to your organization or OUs. The<br>permissions needed to deploy across accounts will automatically be handled by<br>StackSets. For more information, see [Managing stacks across accounts and<br>Regions with StackSets](what-is-cfnstacksets.md "what-is-cfnstacksets.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | February 11, 2020 |
| Drift Detection for StackSets                                                                 | You can now run drift detection on a stack set and all the stack instances it<br>includes. For more information, see [Performing drift detection on CloudFormation<br>StackSets](stacksets-drift.md "stacksets-drift.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | November 19, 2019 |
| CloudFormation registry now available                                                         | You can now use the CloudFormation console to view private and public resources that<br>are available for use in your account. For more information, see [View the available and<br>activated extensions in the CloudFormation registry](registry-view.md "registry-view.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | November 18, 2019 |
| CloudFormation registry API actions                                                           | The following API actions for managing types in the CloudFormation registry are now<br>available.<br>[DeregisterType](../APIReference/API_DeregisterType.md "../APIReference/API_DeregisterType.md")<br>Removes a type or type version from active use in the CloudFormation<br>registry.<br>[DescribeType](../APIReference/API_DescribeType.md "../APIReference/API_DescribeType.md")<br>Returns detailed information about a registered type.<br>[DescribeTypeRegistration](../APIReference/API_DescribeTypeRegistration.md "../APIReference/API_DescribeTypeRegistration.md")<br>Returns information about a type's registration, including its current<br>status and type and version identifiers.<br>[ListTypeRegistrations](../APIReference/API_ListTypeRegistrations.md "../APIReference/API_ListTypeRegistrations.md")<br>Returns a list of registration request identifiers for the specified<br>type.<br>[ListTypes](../APIReference/API_ListTypes.md "../APIReference/API_ListTypes.md")<br>Returns summary information about types that have been registered with<br>CloudFormation.<br>[ListTypeVersions](../APIReference/API_ListTypeVersions.md "../APIReference/API_ListTypeVersions.md")<br>Returns summary information about the versions of a type.<br>[RegisterType](../APIReference/API_RegisterType.md "../APIReference/API_RegisterType.md")<br>Registers a type with the CloudFormation registry. Registering a type<br>makes it available for use in CloudFormation templates in your<br>AWS account.<br>[SetTypeDefaultVersion](../APIReference/API_SetTypeDefaultVersion.md "../APIReference/API_SetTypeDefaultVersion.md")<br>Specify the default version of a type. The default version of a type<br>will be used in CloudFormation operations.<br>For more information about the CloudFormation registry, see [Managing extensions with the<br>CloudFormation registry](registry.md "registry.md") | November 18, 2019 |
| Resource import added                                                                         | If you created an AWS resource outside of CloudFormation management, you can bring<br>this existing resource into CloudFormation management using `resource import`.<br>For more information, see [Import AWS resources into a CloudFormation<br>stack with a resource import](resource-import.md "resource-import.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | November 11, 2019 |
| Stack set limit increases                                                                     | You can now create a maximum of 100 stack sets in your administrator account,<br>create a maximum of 2000 stack instances per stack set, and run a maximum of 3500<br>stack instance operations in each region at the same time, per administrator account.<br>For more information, see [Understand CloudFormation<br>quotas](cloudformation-limits.md "cloudformation-limits.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | August 2, 2019    |
| Limit for resources in concurrent stack operations                                            | CloudFormation now enforces an account limit for the number of resources in concurrent<br>stack operations. This limit is determined by region. For more information, see<br>[Understand<br>CloudFormation quotas](cloudformation-limits.md "cloudformation-limits.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | April 30, 2019    |
| Stack instance operation limit                                                                | For StackSets, you can now have a maximum of 1500 stack instance operations<br>running in a given region at the same time, per administrator account. For more<br>information, see [Understand CloudFormation<br>quotas](cloudformation-limits.md "cloudformation-limits.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | December 13, 2018 |
| The CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND capability is now available                                        | You can now use the `CAPABILITY_AUTO_EXPAND` capability to create or<br>update a stack directly from a stack template that contains macros, without first<br>reviewing the resulting changes in a change set first. For more information, see<br>[CreateStack](../APIReference/API_CreateStack.md "../APIReference/API_CreateStack.md")<br>or [UpdateStack](../APIReference/API_UpdateStack.md "../APIReference/API_UpdateStack.md")<br>in _AWS CloudFormation API Reference_.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | December 7, 2018  |
| Stack drift detection added                                                                   | You can now detect whether a stack's actual configuration has drifted from its<br>expected template configuration as defined within CloudFormation. You can detect drift on<br>an entire stack, or individual stack resources. For more information, see [Detect unmanaged<br>configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection](using-cfn-stack-drift.md "using-cfn-stack-drift.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | November 13, 2018 |
| secretsmanager dynamic reference now available                                                | You can now use the `secretsmanager` dynamic reference to retrieve<br>entire secrets or secret values that are stored in AWS Secrets Manager. Secrets can be database<br>credentials, passwords, third-party API keys, and even arbitrary text. Using the<br>`secretsmanager` dynamic reference guarantees that neither Secrets Manager nor<br>CloudFormation logs or persists any resolved secret value. For more information, see<br>[Get a secret or secret value from Secrets Manager](dynamic-references-secretsmanager.md "dynamic-references-secretsmanager.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | November 9, 2018  |
| Macros now available                                                                          | You can now use macros to perform custom processing on templates, from simple<br>actions like find-and-replace operations to extensive transformations of entire<br>templates. For more information, see [Perform custom processing on CloudFormation<br>templates with template macros](template-macros.md "template-macros.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | September 6, 2018 |
| CloudFormation now supports VPC endpoints powered by PrivateLink                              | You can use a VPC endpoint to create a private connection between your VPC and<br>CloudFormation without requiring access over the Internet, through a NAT instance, a VPN<br>connection, or Direct Connect. For more information, see [Access CloudFormation using an interface<br>endpoint (AWS PrivateLink)](vpc-interface-endpoints.md "vpc-interface-endpoints.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | August 22, 2018   |
| Dynamic references support secure strings                                                     | You can now use new dynamic references to specify values that are stored and<br>managed in other services, including Systems Manager Parameter Store `SecureString`<br>type parameters, in your stack templates. For more information, see [Get a secure string value from Systems Manager Parameter Store](dynamic-references-ssm-secure-strings.md "dynamic-references-ssm-secure-strings.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | August 16, 2018   |
| Stack sets now support customized execution roles                                             | You can now use customized execution roles in target accounts to control the stack<br>resources that users or groups can include in their stack sets. For more information,<br>see [Set up advanced permissions options for stack set operations](stacksets-prereqs-self-managed.md#stacksets-prereqs-advanced-perms "stacksets-prereqs-self-managed.md#stacksets-prereqs-advanced-perms").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | May 30, 2018      |
| Selective updates of stack instances                                                          | You can now use the optional `Accounts` and `Regions`<br>parameters to specify the accounts and regions in which to update stack instances<br>during a stack set update operation. For more information, see [UpdateStackSet](../APIReference/API_UpdateStackSet.md "../APIReference/API_UpdateStackSet.md")<br>in the _CloudFormation API Reference_.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | May 30, 2018      |
| CloudFormation now creates S3 buckets with encryption enabled                                 | For Amazon S3 buckets that CloudFormation creates to store uploaded stack templates,<br>server-side encryption is now enabled by default, thereby encrypting all objects<br>stored in those buckets. For more information, see [Create a stack from the CloudFormation<br>console](cfn-console-create-stack.md "cfn-console-create-stack.md").                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | May 24, 2018      |
| FIPS endpoints added                                                                          | CloudFormation now offers new endpoints which use FIPS 140-2 validated cryptographic<br>modules in the following public US regions: US-East-1, US-East-2, US-West-1, and<br>US-West-2. See [CloudFormation endpoints and quotas](../../../general/latest/gr/cfn.md "../../../general/latest/gr/cfn.md")<br>in the \*Amazon Web Services General Reference<br>• for the new FIPS-compliant endpoint<br>URLs.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | May 17, 2018      |

For updates to the _CloudFormation Hooks User Guide_, see [Document history for the CloudFormation Hooks User Guide](../../../cloudformation-cli/latest/hooks-userguide/doc-history.md "../../../cloudformation-cli/latest/hooks-userguide/doc-history.md") in the _CloudFormation Hooks User
Guide_.

For cache behaviors, use the<br>`CachedMethods` property to specify which methods<br>Amazon CloudFront (CloudFront) caches responses for. For origins, use the<br>`OriginPath` to specify a path that CloudFront uses to<br>request content.<br>[AWS::ElastiCache::CacheCluster](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-elasticache-cachecluster.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-elasticache-cachecluster.md")<br>For Memcached cache clusters, use the `AZMode` and<br>`PreferredAvailabilityZones` properties to specify<br>nodes in multiple Availability Zones (AZs).<br>[AWS::EC2::Volume](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-volume.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-volume.md")<br>Use the `KmsKeyId` property to specify a customer managed key<br>for encrypted volumes.<br>[AWS::OpsWorks::Instance](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-opsworks-instance.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-opsworks-instance.md")<br>Use the `TimeBasedAutoScaling` property to<br>automatically scale instances based on a schedule that you<br>specify.<br>[AWS::OpsWorks::Layer](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-opsworks-layer.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-opsworks-layer.md")<br>Use the `LoadBasedAutoScaling` property to specify<br>load-based scaling policies. second,<br>respectively.<br>[AWS::RDS::DBInstance](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-rds-dbinstance.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-rds-dbinstance.md")<br>Use the `CharacterSetName` property to hosted<br>zones.<br>Use the `HostedZoneTags` property to associate tags<br>with hosted zones. | New feature                                                               | February 2, 2012   | CloudFormation now provides support for resources in an existing Amazon Virtual Private Cloud<br>(Amazon VPC). With this release, you can:<br>• Launch an EC2 Dedicated instance into an existing Amazon VPC. For more<br>information, see [AWS::EC2::Instance](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-instance.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-instance.md").<br>• Set the `SourceDestCheck` attribute of an EC2 instance<br>that resides in an existing Amazon VPC. For more information, see [AWS::EC2::Instance](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-instance.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-instance.md").<br>• Create Elastic IP addresses in an existing Amazon VPC. For more<br>information, see [AWS::EC2::EIP](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-eip.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-eip.md").<br>• Use CloudFormation to create Amazon VPC security groups and ingress/egress<br>rules in an existing VPC. For more information, see [AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-securitygroup.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-securitygroup.md").<br>• Associate an Auto Scaling group with an existing Amazon VPC by setting the<br>`VPCZoneIdentifier` property of your<br>`AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup` resource. For more<br>information, see [AWS::AutoScaling::AutoScalingGroup](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-autoscaling-autoscalinggroup.md").<br>• Attach an ELB load balancer to a Amazon VPC subnet and create security<br>groups for the load balancer. For more information, see [AWS::ElasticLoadBalancing::LoadBalancer](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-elasticloadbalancing-loadbalancer.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-elasticloadbalancing-loadbalancer.md").<br>• Create an RDS DB instance in an existing Amazon VPC. For more<br>information, see [AWS::RDS::DBInstance](../TemplateReference/aws-resource-rds-dbinstance.md "../TemplateReference/aws-resource-rds-dbinstance.md").
